Patient-reported symptoms:
  Negative Appraisals: World is Dangerous: The world is a dangerous place, Constant Vigilance: I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next, Self-Blame: The event happened because of the way I acted

Vignette:
Kofi had always been a private person, but after the stalking incident last year, he began to feel like he was constantly looking over his shoulder. It started when he met a girl at a design conference in New York City. They exchanged numbers and went on a few dates, but things quickly took a dark turn. She became possessive and controlling, showing up at his work and sending him hundreds of texts a day. Kofi tried to brush it off as clinginess, but when she started showing up at his apartment building, he knew he had to take action. The final straw was when he came home from a late-night design project to find her waiting in the lobby, furious that he hadn't responded to her messages. She confronted him in front of his neighbors, and Kofi felt a surge of fear and helplessness. He managed to shake her off and filed a restraining order, but the incident left him shaken. As time went on, Kofi became increasingly convinced that the world was a dangerous place. He started to vary his daily routine, taking different routes to work and avoiding crowded areas. He began to feel like he had to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next. He would scan the room before entering, looking for potential escape routes or hiding spots. Kofi couldn't shake the feeling that the stalking incident was somehow his fault. He replayed their conversations in his head, wondering if there was something he could have done differently to prevent it. He became withdrawn and isolated, avoiding social events and canceling plans with friends. His design work began to suffer as well, as he found himself preoccupied with thoughts of safety and security. As a UX designer, Kofi's job required him to be observant and attentive to detail. But now, his hypervigilance made it difficult for him to focus on anything else. He would catch himself scanning the office for potential threats or imagining worst-case scenarios. His coworkers noticed a change in him and started to ask if everything was okay. One day, Kofi's boss called him into her office to discuss a project he had been working on. She mentioned that his recent designs had been lacking their usual creativity and flair. Kofi broke down in tears, finally opening up about the stalking incident and how it had affected him. His boss listened attentively, offering support and resources. For the first time since the incident, Kofi felt like he could talk about what had happened without fear of judgment or rejection. He realized that he needed help to process his emotions and work through his negative appraisals. With his boss's encouragement, Kofi decided to seek therapy, hoping to regain control over his life and learn to navigate the world without constant fear. As he sat in the therapist's waiting room, Kofi couldn't help but think about all the what-ifs. What if he had never met her? What if he had reported her behavior sooner? He knew it wouldn't be easy, but he was ready to face his fears and work towards a more balanced life.
